name: Social Visit Pass (tourist) / eVisa

requirements.blocker_text: Many nationalities enter visa-free for stays of 30-90 days depending on nationality, or via the eVisa/eNTRI online system; other nationalities need a consular Social Visit Pass.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for a Social Visit Pass at a Malaysian embassy or consulate if not visa-exempt or eVisa eligible.

requirements.blocker_text: Covers tourism, social visits, and short business meetings; does not authorise employment.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for the relevant work or pass category instead if the purpose is employment.

evidence_required.document: Proof of onward travel and sufficient funds

outcome.duration_length: 30-90 days depending on nationality and entry type

sources.title: Malaysia.gov.my (rai.malaysia.gov.my, official government portal) -- entry and pass category overview, confirming Social Visit Pass, eVISA, VTR, and MDAC mechanisms directly

notes: Malaysia's federal structure has a real, practical effect even on this baseline visit category: Sabah and Sarawak (East Malaysia) retain their own immigration authority under the Malaysia Agreement 1963, and travellers -- including Malaysians from the Peninsula -- must pass a separate immigration checkpoint when moving between Peninsular Malaysia and either East Malaysian state, or between Sabah and Sarawak themselves. A visa or pass valid for Peninsular Malaysia does not automatically grant entry to Sabah/Sarawak and vice versa -- this distinction runs through nearly every route in the Malaysia build and is documented in detail on the MM2H-family route files, where it has the most consequential effect.
